title: Timed mini-section: Zam Zam Laundry (16 marks, 20 minutes)
subject: Business
source: Written for business/y11 lesson 56 (Mini-section with mark scheme (teacher-written, pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 56. Read the case first (3 minutes). About a minute per mark. Use a calculator; show working.

passage.title: Zam Zam Laundry Ltd (fictional)
paras: Zam Zam Laundry Ltd is a small laundry and dry cleaner in east London owned by Bilal Rahman. It has 8 staff and is known for quick, careful service. Last year its revenue was £180,000; this year it was £207,000.

A national chain has opened a branch on the same high street with lower prices and an app. Bilal is considering two options: a collection and delivery service using one electric van, or opening a second branch in a nearby town. Customers say speed and trust matter most to them.

questions.a: The proportion (percentage) of total sales in a market made by one business (1 for sales of the market, 1 for one business's share).

questions.q: Explain one benefit to Zam Zam Laundry of a collection and delivery service.
questions.a: 1 benefit identified (for example more convenient for busy customers); 1 developed (so more customers choose it over the chain); 1 in context (customers value speed and trust, and the chain only offers an app).

questions.q: Explain one risk to Zam Zam Laundry of opening a second branch.
questions.a: 1 risk (for example high fixed costs such as rent); 1 development (cash is tied up and break-even rises); 1 context (Bilal faces new competition, so revenue may not grow enough).

questions.q: Analyse the impact on Zam Zam Laundry of competition from the national chain.
questions.a: Levels (6-mark analyse): Level 3 (5 to 6) two developed chains in context, for example lower prices may take customers, so revenue growth of 15% may slow, which means less cash for the van; but Zam Zam's trust and speed may keep loyal customers, so it could compete on service rather than price.

questions.q: Calculate the percentage change in Zam Zam Laundry's revenue.
